account:
Today I am keeping my appointments while trying to understand the hospitality arrangements being organized around me. I am at the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection, but have not yet received a report on grain stocks or deliveries. A townsman has just said, "bridge or port change at bakery." I do not yet understand what he means or whether it relates to the gathering.

The unusual business is tonight's eighteen o'clock meeting in the town hall great hall. The innkeeper requested it, specifically asking that my secretary escort me. I approved thirty minutes. The innkeeper says the committee consists of the innkeeper, builder, and freight operator, and that they will discuss refreshments, deliveries, and hall lighting for community gatherings. Residents are welcome and supposedly need not prepare. The neighbour has said they plan to attend. My secretary has confirmed the appointment and intends to escort me.

The strongest reason for further questions is the baker's report, relayed by my secretary, that the committee ordered 120 loaves baked yesterday, with payment still unconfirmed. That seems a substantial provision for a short discussion. Neither my secretary nor I has authorized treasury payment. I asked her to establish who placed the order, its intended use, and who agreed to pay, and supplied a writable book for recording the answers. I also saw a lantern installed in the great hall yesterday, which might fit the stated lighting arrangements, though I do not know who installed it or why.

My working explanation is that the committee is preparing an actual community gathering, possibly something more elaborate than the brief planning meeting they have described. I feel there may be preparations I have not been told about, but I have no evidence of wrongdoing or a confirmed hidden purpose. I should distinguish their stated hospitality agenda from my suspicions, obtain the bread and payment details, clarify the bakery remark, and attend the scheduled meeting.
